VERDICT: ACCEPT

The argument holds. Complementary pairs $\{A, S\setminus A\}$ give an upper bound of $2^{999}$, and the transversals $A$ with $A' = S\setminus A$ force their pairs out of $P$, giving $2^{999}-2^{499}$. The construction (all sets of size $\ge 501$, plus one orbit from each good complementary pair of 500-sets) meets this bound and satisfies both conditions. The final number is $2^{499}(2^{500}-1)$, and its digit sum (1392 ≡ 6 mod 9) matches the expected residue. Its 301-digit length and leading digits also match $2^{999}$.

CONFIDENCE: 4
